correctness.rationale: The normalized centered Hermite ambiguity functions are A h_j(x,ξ)=exp(−τ/2)L_j(τ) for τ=π(x²+ξ²), with L1=1−τ and L2=1−2τ+τ²/2. The true Gaussian-relative weighted squared gain is F_w(τ)=wL1²+(1−w)L2², w∈[0,1], τ≥0. At τ0=3−sqrt5, L1(τ0)=sqrt5−2 and L2(τ0)=−(sqrt5−2), so every w obeys inf F_w≤9−4sqrt5. For w*=1−1/sqrt5, the exact certificate F_w*−(9−4sqrt5)=(sqrt5/20)(τ−τ0)²((τ−1−sqrt5)²+4) is nonnegative on all reals with unique equality radius; independently verified symbolic difference identically zero. Differentiating at interior τ0 forces unique optimal w*. The Gaussian factor decays, so theorem is only Gaussian-relative, not uniform unweighted inversion; no global nonlinear STFT phase-reconstruction guarantee.
